newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Howard says Australian budget not treading water.
newsitem.headline: Howard says Australian budget not treading water.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard defended his government on Wednesday against claims that it was only treading water in its 1997/98 (July/June) budget.

"How can you be treading water when you've laid down the circumstances for a surplus of A$1.6 billion, when you're repaying A$5 billion of debt and you're creating the circumstances for low interest rates -- that's not treading water," Howard told Perth radio station 6PR.
The budget, released on Tuesday, projects a A$3.9 billion underlying deficit in 1997/98, improving to a A$1.6 billion surplus in 1998/99.
The government's net borrowing requirement was forecast at negative A$5.2 billion in 1997/98, with the funds being used to retire debt.
Financial markets and media commentators were generally disappointed with the outcome, having expected the 1997/98 deficit to be lower than was announced.
Howard said apart from the deficit reduction, other measures such as a tax incentive on savings and funds for infrastracture projects showed it was not a budget of inactivity.
"That's not treading water, it is swimming freestyle dramatically, he said.
